newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Barrage of data lurks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Barrage of data lurks.

text.p: U.S. credit markets next week will contend with a statistical storm that has the potential to wreak havoc across the Treasury yield curve.
The good news is that government bond prices will likely bear the wrath of the data deluge largely unscathed, Wall Street money market experts said.
"If my (forecast) numbers come out to be the case ... it would not change the market tone," said Cheryl Katz, a senior economist at Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
Katz said the market tone is benign because the econonmy continues to grow at a healthy pace without the threat of inflationary pressures.
"My forecast would coincide with that view," the economist said.

Top-tier data to be released next week include second-quarter employment cost index (ECI) Tuesday, advanced second-quarter reading on Gross Domestic Product (GDP) Thursday, and July payrolls and June personal income and consumption Friday.
